speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; the pattern of a previous swollen ankle followed by current right knee and urinary symptoms is quite specific. To understand the severity and duration of your current flare-up, have you noticed any fever or chills accompanying the knee pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (Reiter's Syndrome). Given the classic triad of asymmetric oligoarthritis (ankle then knee), urethritis (pain with urination), and risk factors (unprotected sex), this is highly suggestive of reactive arthritis. I will now request relevant imaging and labs to confirm the diagnosis and rule out septic arthritis. REQUEST IMAGES: Right_Knee_XRay, Right_Knee_Ultrasound. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Culture, HLA-B27, Synovial_Fluid_Analysis, CBC, CRP, ESR.
